disposition_mapping.rationale: Claim submission persists as the employee-facing entry point and still consumes receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold; it is merged with the former receipt capture step since extraction now happens inline at submission.
Receipt capture and data extraction is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into submission via real-time OCR in the self-service app, eliminating the separate AP analyst handling step.

The policy compliance check survives as required (EXR-R-07) but is restructured from a manual AP analyst check into an automated rules-engine check with analyst oversight; it still precedes manager approval, satisfying the ordering requirement.

Line manager approval survives as required (EXR-R-08), remains distinct from the submitting employee (actor separation, EXR-R-03) and still follows the policy check (EXR-R-02); it is restructured to be exception-aware, with system-flagged lines surfaced for manager attention.

Finance review is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into the automated posting step as an exception-triggered control, removing the universal manual review while preserving human judgment for flagged coding or evidentiary issues.

Posting still consumes the expense transaction date (EXR-R-04) and transaction-date exchange rate (EXR-R-05) and is merged with the former finance review step into a single automated posting control with embedded exception handling.

Reimbursement survives as required (EXR-R-09) and still occurs after line manager approval (EXR-R-06, via TS-03 preceding TS-05 through TS-04); it is merged with employee notification into a single automated payment-and-notify step.
Employee notification is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into the reimbursement step, with the payment system triggering notification automatically once payment clears.

steps.description: The employee submits an out-of-pocket expense claim through a self-service app that performs real-time OCR capture and data extraction on attached receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold, producing a structured claim record at the point of submission.
inputs: Receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold
steps.name: Claim submission with automated receipt capture

steps.description: A policy rules engine checks every claim line against expense policy limits, categories and per diem rates automatically, flagging non-compliant or exception lines; an AP analyst oversees the engine's rule configuration and triages flagged exceptions.
steps.name: Automated policy compliance check

steps.description: The claimant's line manager reviews the policy-checked claim, with system-highlighted exceptions surfaced for closer scrutiny, and approves or rejects the claim.
steps.name: Line manager approval (exception-aware)

steps.description: The approved claim is posted automatically to expense accounts and cost centres in the period the expense was incurred, translating foreign-currency lines using the transaction-date exchange rate; a finance reviewer intervenes only on system-flagged coding anomalies, policy exceptions or weak evidentiary support, replacing the former universal manual finance review with exception-based oversight.
steps.name: Automated posting with embedded finance exception review

steps.description: The posted claim is paid to the employee through the AP payment run, and the payment system automatically notifies the employee once reimbursement has cleared.
steps.name: Automated reimbursement and notification
